annotations.keyFindings: A written dose-adjustment plan given at pre-assessment was followed by fewer out-of-range day-of-surgery values (34 to 21 percent) and fewer infusions (46 to 18 percent), with similar postoperative hypoglycaemia.
annotations.notes: Planning value for the primary outcome.

annotations.keyFindings: A pilot trial of a pre-surgery nurse call met its recruitment criterion (48 percent) but not outcome completeness (79 against 90 percent), because ward capillary values were not documented.
annotations.notes: Shows what threatens a local trial.

annotations.keyFindings: First-on-the-list scheduling was achieved for 71 percent of general surgery, 38 percent of orthopaedic and 64 percent of urology patients.
annotations.notes: Less relevant now that orthopaedic lists cannot move patients: scheduling applies to general surgery and urology only.

annotations.keyFindings: Correction scales were associated with less hypoglycaemia than infusions for operations under three hours (4 against 9 percent).
Perioperative glucose above 10 to 12 mmol/L was associated with surgical site infection (odds ratio 1.8); small trials of tighter control did not reduce infection.
annotations.notes: Supports the outcome threshold, not the protocol.

annotations.keyFindings: Patients described conflicting insulin advice, changed insulin on their own for fear of hypoglycaemia, and valued one written plan and a named contact.
annotations.notes: Supports a patient-reported outcome on instructions.

annotations.keyFindings: Meters were accurate above 5.5 mmol/L but read high below 4 mmol/L, especially with low haematocrit.
annotations.notes: Low meter values need laboratory confirmation.

claims.text: A written insulin dose-adjustment plan at pre-assessment was followed by fewer patients with out-of-range glucose on the day of surgery.
claims.passage: Out-of-range glucose on the day of surgery, defined as a capillary value above 12 or below 4 mmol/L, fell from 34 percent to 21 percent.
claims.interpretation: Planning values for the outcome; uncontrolled.

claims.text: A pilot trial of pre-surgery nurse calls recruited 48 percent of eligible patients but documented outcomes for only 79 percent.
claims.passage: Outcome data were complete for 79 percent, below the 90 percent criterion, mainly because capillary values were not documented on the ward.
claims.interpretation: Recruitment and outcome completeness are the risks for any local trial.

claims.text: First-on-the-list scheduling was achieved for only 38 percent of orthopaedic patients with diabetes.
claims.passage: First-on-the-list scheduling was achieved for 71 percent of general surgery patients, 38 percent of orthopaedic patients and 64 percent of urology patients.
claims.interpretation: Consistent with the investigator's constraint; scheduling cannot be a universal component.

claims.text: For operations under three hours, subcutaneous correction scales were associated with less hypoglycaemia than variable-rate infusions.
claims.passage: Hypoglycaemia below 4 mmol/L within 24 hours occurred in 4 percent with the correction scale and 9 percent with the infusion.
claims.interpretation: Supports replacing routine infusions for short operations.

claims.text: Patients valued a single written plan followed by all staff and a named person to call.
claims.passage: Participants valued a single written plan that all staff followed and a named person to call.
claims.interpretation: A patient-reported measure of consistent instructions belongs in the evaluation.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level against the revised constraints. A pre-assessment dose plan was followed by fewer out-of-range values (34 to 21 percent) and correction scales by less hypoglycaemia than infusions, both in observational studies. A pilot trial of a nurse call recruited adequately but failed on outcome completeness because ward values were not documented. First-on-the-list scheduling is unreliable in orthopaedics, which matches the new constraint. Patients want one plan and one contact. Low meter readings need laboratory confirmation.
gradeRationale: Observational before-after and cohort evidence, one small pilot trial and qualitative data; consistent direction, serious risk of bias and imprecision.
summary: Seven retrieved records appraised against the revised constraints; five claims recorded; certainty low.
